judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-5 Content statements (rank 4) under the same Competency C-2.3 (four operations applied to real-life problems) and Curricular Goal CG-2 (fluency with whole numbers, place value, four operations). The first specifies multi-digit multiplication procedures (three-digit x two-digit; four-digit x single-digit, per its LCs), while the second covers understanding powers of 10 and performing all four operations on them (LCs: add/subtract/multiply/divide powers of 10). Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (26 and 33 omitted items), so absence of explicit dependency language in the excerpts is not proof of absence, but the available text supports only symmetric conceptual coherence.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-1.4 ('Observes, identifies, and extends basic patterns in everyday surroundings') but at different resolved Class coordinates: 'Patterns in body movements (shape and position)' at Class-1 (rank 0) and 'Block patterns' at Class-2 (rank 1), so any developmental direction must run first_to_second. The Class-1 LCs (observe / identify / extend patterns in body movements based on shape and position) establish the core pattern skills of recognising a repeating unit and continuing it using shape and position cues in a concrete, enactive medium; the Class-2 LCs (observe and identify block patterns; extend block patterns) apply the same observe–identify–extend cycle to spatial arrangements of blocks, a more abstract and manipulable representation with structured shape/position configurations. This is substantive extension of the same pattern competency into a new, more demanding representation rather than mere repetition of wording, so Class-1 proficiency plausibly supports success at Class-2. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and shared ancestors carry merge/audit context and lack developmental coordinates, so the judgment rests on the endpoint descriptions, LCs, and resolved Class coordinates only.

judgment.rationale: Both are Content SFIs under the same Competency C-3.1 ('identifies, compares and analyzes attributes of two- and three-dimensional shapes') and Curricular Goal CG-3, with resolved coordinates Class-3 (rank 2) and Class-4 (rank 3), so only first_to_second is developmentally permitted. The Class-3 content and its LCs establish properties of squares, rectangles, triangles and circles in terms of sides and corners; the Class-4 content and its LCs require making a cube, cuboid and cylinder from nets, i.e. assembling plane figures (squares, rectangles, circles) into solids. Secure knowledge of the constituent 2-D figures and their side/corner properties substantively supports recognising and folding the correct nets, a genuine extension from plane-figure attributes to 3-D construction rather than mere repetition. Both endpoints carry upstream audit/merge context and truncated source evidence (24 omitted evidence items each), which limits but does not contradict this reading.

judgment.rationale: Both are Class-3 Content statements (rank 2, gap 0) under the same Competency C-2.3 ('Visualises and recognizes relationships among operations and applies the four basic operations...'). The first is conceptual/relational ('Recognises the relationship between addition and subtraction through contexts and activity', LC tags addition/subtraction/inverse/relationship); the second is procedural range-bounded computation ('Addition and subtraction up to 999', LCs 'Add whole numbers up to 999' / 'Subtract whole numbers up to 999'). These are genuinely complementary within the same operations strand — inverse-relationship understanding supports checking and flexible computation, while computational work with three-digit numbers provides contexts for seeing the relationship — but the bounded source evidence gives no substantive basis for asserting a same-rank developmental direction either way, and neither statement extends, broadens, or increases the complexity of the other. Shared wording ('addition', 'subtraction'), same parent, same source page, and equal rank alone do not establish dependency, so symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment.
